text:
Maya: quick sync — we need a concrete rollback experiment plan for the next pin/retire wave. customers asking for predictable cutovers; want repeatable tactics we can copy across tenants.
Alex: agreed. want a minimal checklist: canary size, monitoring window, rollback triggers, comms?
Sam: rough plan: 1% traffic canary or single-customer canary, 48h probe for perf/stability, collect latencies, token-cost delta, and eval set quality.
Jamie: add a semantic drift probe: sample 500 prompts, compute embed similarity vs baseline. rollback if average similarity drops >6% or user-facing error-rate >0.4%.
Maya: good. need operator steps spelled out so on-call can flip rollouts and confirm fallback.
Alex: propose two rollback paths: soft-fallback (route affected requests to previous pinned model) and hard-rollback (re-pin across tenant + notify customer). soft for transient regressions, hard for sustained/major regressions.
Sam: soft-fallback implemented via routing policy priority lists. example config we'll use in playbook:
```
route_policy:
  - model: model-v3-q8
    priority: 40
  - model: model-v2-stable
    priority: 100
fallback: true
```
Jamie: nice. how do we decide automated hard-rollback vs manual?
Maya: start manual for first 4 tenants; collect signal reliability. if thresholds prove robust over 3 experiments we can enable auto-hard-rollback behind a flag.
ops: manual playbook (high level): 1) pause rollout (CLI) 2) set routing to v2-stable 3) run smoke tests (sample prompts) 4) update comms and tickets. I'll add exact commands later.
Alex: can we add a dry-run mode for rehearsals that logs decisions but doesn't change routing?
Sam: yes — add `--dry-run` to rollout CLI and a `decision-log` output that lists tenant ids, affected routes, and top failing prompts.
Maya: timeline: run two experiments this quarter — one single-tenant, one 5-tenant burst. goal: reduce manual escalations by 50% and validate semantic drift threshold.
Jamie: measurement plan: latency p50/p95, token-cost delta, semantic similarity delta, user error-rate, and support ticket volume. snapshot pre/post for reproducibility.
Alex: owners: eng-runtime for routing changes (Alex), eng-sre for alerts (Jamie), ops for playbook (ops), canary infra (Sam). Maya will own consolidating results and comms.
deploy-bot: Canary infra change (dry-run flag) scheduled: 2026-04-08T02:00:00Z.
Maya: action items:
- Alex: implement dry-run + decision logging (due 2026-04-01)
- Jamie: finalize semantic drift probe and threshold (due 2026-03-28)
- Sam: stand up 1% pipeline + exporter (due 2026-04-02)
- ops: write manual rollback playbook + commands (due 2026-03-30)
- Maya: draft customer comms and risk matrix (due 2026-03-30)
Sam: I'll add a helper script to extract failing prompts: `./canary-analyze --tenant $T --since 48h --top 5` and wire it into logs.
Jamie: recommend alert rules: PagerDuty if semantic drop >6% AND support volume spike >25% over baseline; Slack-only for single-signal blips.
Maya: blockers?
Alex: infra quota for canaries; filed request with infra team.
ops: prepping playbook now, no blockers.
Sam: quota request sent, awaiting approval.
Jamie: eval side is clear.
Maya: thanks, this is actionable. we'll reconvene next Tue to review progress. @everyone add any blockers below. :eyes:
